question: Why did the gap between men's and women's elite running times stop shrinking in the 1980s?
answer: Because much of the earlier narrowing was catch-up, and some was drugs. Seiler, De Koning and Foster studied Olympic and world finals from 1952 to 2006: the gap fell as women gained coaching and races, bottomed out in the 1980s, then widened slightly once out-of-competition drug testing arrived. It now sits around 10 to 12%.
move: When a trend flattens, ask what was driving it before.
ask: Is a gap I am trying to close shrinking through real change, or has that change already run out?
source: Seiler, De Koning & Foster, Med Sci Sports Exerc, 2007
reference: Stephen Seiler, Jos J. De Koning & Carl Foster, The Fall and Rise of the Gender Difference in Elite Anaerobic Performance 1952–2006, Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise, 2007
